law.label: Boyle's law: a closed swim bladder shrinks with depth (pressure p0 + rho g d)
law.statement_en: With absolute pressure p0 + rho g d (surface pressure p0, water density rho and gravity g as named hypotheses) and P(d) V(d) constant (closed bladder, fixed temperature, quasi-static), the bladder volume at depth d is V(0) p0 / (p0 + rho g d); a closed bladder claiming more volume at depth is ruled out. The v1 '1 atm per 10 m' law is the instance rho g = 10132.5 Pa/m (oneAtmPer10m).

hypotheses.name: Delphi.Hydro.WaterColumn
hypotheses.statement: p0 > 0, rho > 0, g > 0; P(d) = p0 + rho g d
hypotheses.source: hydrostatics; sea water 1025 kg/m^3 and fresh water 998.2 kg/m^3 (NIST) as the engine's pressure scenario cites them; 1 atm per 10 m (Yancey 2020) is the instance rho g = 10132.5 Pa/m

hypotheses.name: hboyle
hypotheses.statement: P(d) V(d) = c for every d >= 0 (closed bladder, fixed temperature, quasi-static; fails for rapid decompression, Kerr et al. 2023)

scope.basis: gas physics (Boyle) in a water column of committed density and gravity; quasi-static only (Kerr et al. 2023)

sources: sim-engine/scenarios/pressure.mjs (rho_w 1025 sea water, 998.2 fresh water NIST, g 9.80665)
observations: v1 (k fixed at 0.1 atm/m) called a correct Boyle volume violated in sea water: 1025 x 9.80665 = 10053 Pa/m < 10132.5 Pa/m, so the real volume sits 0.5 to 1 percent above the v1 bound
